cards.title: Your 23 tiers, wired
cards.text: All 23 tiers you kept are in, spaced out, and alike ones now differ by finish, cut or motion, not just colour.
cards.why: Your notes: tin and copper (and every similar set) should be more than a colour swap, and space them out. Mark any group or film that's off.
cards.details:
To update: close Primer fully and open it again; Profile shows the new version at the bottom.

Plain is still below wood. Bronze is gone (copper takes its place). The ones you didn't tick (bronze, clay, stone, rose gold, jade, legendary, prism, omnipotent) are kept aside, drawn but never reached, so any can come back.

Why these gaps: a run starts at ×0 each time and a review is about 10 to 30 questions. A short run that goes well still reaches a few tiers (five by 17). Past that, a big review keeps reaching a new tier every 6 to 16 answers, and void needs 179 right in a row in one run, about six whole reviews without a break.

Shields as you said: wood and tin none, copper to gold one, platinum and up two, refilled at every new tier. I weighed a third for the far end and left it out: with two back at every tier the top is already forgiving enough.

Each group's first film shows them side by side; the rest are one tier each, six seconds, looping, shown bigger than on the phone, at a count in its range. Singularity took omnipotent's black-hole drawing, since a singularity is a black hole; eclipse is drawn new.

parts.title: Wood and the metals
parts.text: Wood: grain and a knot, still. Tin: matte grey with a few dents, nothing shines. Copper: warm, verdigris crusting its bottom edge and a corner, a slow warm sheen. Silver: polished, a fine bright line, a quick white sweep. Gold: a raised rim like a coin's, a warm sweep, a glow. Platinum: a mirror, bright sky over a sharp dark horizon, a faint rainbow sweep. Titanium: brushed lines with an anodised rainbow edge.

parts.title: The gems
parts.text: Each cut its own way. Emerald: long steps round a wide table, corners cut, the light walking slowly along the steps. Sapphire: a polished dome with a six-rayed star gliding over it. Crystal: a cluster of points standing up, glints on the tips. Ruby: the princess cut, rings of facets closing on the middle, an ember breathing inside. Diamond: the brilliant, its fire and quick sparkles.

parts.title: The dark stones
parts.text: Obsidian: black glass with the curved ripples of where it broke, a violet sheen sweeping. Opal: milky, pastel drifting through, flecks of bright colour flashing in turn.

parts.title: The sky
parts.text: Aurora keeps its ribbons and rim spark. Nebula is soft pink and blue clouds drifting the other way, thick with stars. Celestial: a gold constellation, gold rim and a gold spark circling. Eternal: white gold with pale rays turning and a figure-of-eight spark.

parts.title: The far end
parts.text: Supernova bursts outward in rings. Eclipse (new): a black moon over the sun, its corona and a bead of light flaring on its edge. Singularity is now the black hole, in violet, sparks spiralling in. Multiverse: copies of the chip drifting out of step. Void: nothing but drifting stars.

parts.title: Where each starts, and shields
parts.text:
The gap to the next tier grows: 3 for the first three, then 4, 5, 6, 8, 10 and 13 for three tiers each, 16 for the last two.

- Wood at 3, no shields
- Tin at 6, no shields
- Copper at 9, 1 shield
- Silver at 13, 1 shield
- Gold at 17, 1 shield
- Platinum at 21, 2 shields
- Emerald at 26, 2 shields
- Sapphire at 31, 2 shields

A full review of 30 right reaches emerald; void needs 179 in a row in one run.

cards.title: New crack and shatter
cards.text: Three new cracks and three new shatters. Tick one of each you like.
cards.why: You said both old sounds were bad. These are softer and rounder: a tink with a soft body for the crack, a bright cascade over a soft thump for the shatter. My picks are in the app now.
cards.details:
Made here from sine tones and noise, no recordings. Each is levelled to about -27.5 LUFS like the animations' sounds, so they sit well under the voice; they play with Effects on, like the other effects.

The crack plays when a shield takes a miss; the shatter when the combo is lost. If none of the three is right for one of them, say what's off (too high, too sharp, too long) and I'll make another set.

items.label: Crack A: porcelain
items.text: A porcelain tink with a soft knock under it, and two tiny ticks as the crack runs.

items.label: Crack B: glass
items.text: A glass tap, then a second higher, softer one as the crack spreads; a lighter knock.

items.label: Crack C: ceramic
items.text: A lower, warmer cup-like tink with more body, and a short soft scrape.

items.label: Shatter A: cascade
items.text: A soft low thump, a bright break, and small bits cascading away, thinning as they fall.

items.label: Shatter B: chimes
items.text: The same break, its bits falling as notes stepping down a scale, like small chimes.

items.label: Shatter C: shower
items.text: A brighter, quicker shower of fine bits with a soft sparkle of air behind it.
